title: Mindfulness: the 5-4-3-2-1 senses game

How can I calm my busy mind?

explain.say: Right now your mind might be thinking about lunch, or yesterday, or tomorrow's test. Minds love to time-travel! Mindfulness means gently bringing your attention back to right now. Look at the board: a game that uses your five senses.

faq.a: Mindfulness means paying attention to what is happening right now, like your breath, sounds or feelings, in a gentle way without judging them.
It is a calming game using your senses: find five things you see, four you feel, three you hear, two you smell and one you taste. It brings your mind back to now.
Many studies suggest mindfulness helps people feel less stressed and focus better. It is not magic, and it works best with regular practice.

faq.q: What if my mind keeps wandering?
faq.a: That is completely normal; minds wander all the time. Just notice it and gently bring your attention back. Bringing it back is the practice.
asks: I cannot stop thinking during mindfulness

faq.a: Any time: before a test, when you feel worried, at bedtime, or even while eating or walking. A one-minute practice can help.

facts: Jon Kabat-Zinn started a mindfulness course to help people with stress at a hospital in Massachusetts, USA, in 1979.
Studies suggest that regular mindfulness practice can help many people feel less stressed.
